purpose: One shared Mass knowledge layer powers immediate live cues and deeper Formation explanations without creating a separate gestures/postures module.
governing_rule: Mass runtime owns what the user needs now; Mass Formation owns what the action, posture, gesture, sound, position or response means.

source_registries.role: Exact-cue gesture source of truth, including Campion provenance and icon bindings.
Faithful posture transitions and profile-aware posture state.
Persistent priest station/position state for the live right rail and Formation explanation.
Audible/silent/voice-state cues and explanatory links for the liturgical soundscape.
Source-backed Campion rubric-event overlay for exact visible actions and guide hooks.
User-facing explanatory course and source-backed long-form formation owner.

mass_runtime.behavior: Project the minimum useful state at the exact cue; deeper explanation must hand off by reference.

owns: why the priest moves or turns
why parts are audible or silent
how the parts of Mass fit together
historical development where it directly explains the rite
excludes: general apologetics not specific to understanding the Mass
postconciliar controversy whose primary question is continuity or rupture

owns: definition of liturgical and technical terms
standalone historical chronology and case studies when chronology is the main user need
claims about reform, rupture, suppression, change, authority or postconciliar controversy
examples: Did Vatican II require versus populum?
Did the reform weaken sacrificial language?

owns: external objection or defence of Catholic worship
examples: Is the Mass a re-sacrifice of Christ?

migration_policy: Do not duplicate gesture/posture explanations in live Mass cards.
Do not create a top-level Gestures & Postures Formation route.
Use the canonical gesture matrix as gesture authority; reader-gestures remains compatibility projection for faithful gestures.
Campion is explanatory/discovery provenance, while the 1962 Roman Missal remains primary rubrical authority where the priest rubric is normative.
Every new Mass explanation should reference existing cue/registry IDs when possible rather than inventing parallel identifiers.
